newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Report faults Israel jet deal with Pritzkers.
newsitem.headline: Report faults Israel jet deal with Pritzkers.

text.p: A report presented to the Israeli parliament's Finance Committee cast doubt on the terms of a jet-manufacturing deal between Israel Aircraft Industries (IAI) and U.S. family Pritzker, a government source said on Monday.

The report, written by Industry and Trade Ministry's chief scientist and its acting director general Joshua Gleitman, was presented last week to the committee, which voted to approve a $50 million state guarantee for the development of government-owned IAI's Galaxy executive jet.

Terms of the guarantee say that should development of the plane stop or the Galaxy fail to get U.S Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approval by the end of 1998, the government would refund the Chicago-based Pritzkers the $50 million they are investing in the project.
The source said the deal with the Pritzkers was unbalanced, with IAI taking all the risks while owning only 20 percent of the joint venture company set up with the Pritzkers.
The Pritzkers, who own the remaining 80 percent of the company, had reportedly said they would invest in the development of the jet in return for worldwide distribution rights.

In the report, Gleitman supported the guarantee but said the deadlines for building a prototype and conducting test flights were tight, therefore they are vulnerable to delays in the supply of parts or by a workers' strike.

The report said that should the project not meet its 1998 FAA deadline, cancellation of the deal would not only cost the state the $50 million guarantee, but would cost IAI millions of dollars in obligations to subcontractors and suppliers and from the closure of its production department and the laying off of 650 workers.
The report estimated the cost of the further development of the Galaxy and the production of eight planes by December 1998 at $140 million.
